6.​ Amend paragraph 26 (Coventry) 
 
To the extent that it is adopted throughout the British economy, AI will may render previously 
secure sectors redundant. Techno-optimists say AI investment will pay for itself by cutting 
labour costs, replacing up to 40 percent of tasks now done by humans in the not very distant 
future, and pushing jobless rates as high as 20 percent. The latest reports say that AI could 
destroy three million jobs in Britain, including many highly-skilled jobs, in the next decade. In 
reality, this splurge of AI investment may be a modern-day hunt for El Dorado: billions 
have been invested with little to no gain, with MIT finding that 95% of companies are 
yet to see any return on their AI investments. Research by an AI consulting firm found 
that AI tools saved time for senior executives, but not ordinary workers. A senior 
analyst at Gartner said “most layoffs right now aren’t actually happening due to AI 
[successes]… the layoffs seem to be part of a broader strategy to reinvest funds in AI, 
hoping for success down the line”, with the same firm anticipating that half of jobs 
cut for AI-related reasons will be rehired by 2027. Much of this research is from the 
US, which is leagues ahead of the UK in terms of AI investment. In contrast, OpenAI 
has backed out of investing £31bn in Britain due to high energy costs and 
“regulation”. AI has huge potential as a tool to aid economic planning, but the 
technology is still immature. AI’s immediate threat to jobs may instead come from the 
bubble bursting, with the crisis in the stock market exposing the crisis in the real 
economy. In either case, without a planned economy, labour-saving technology creates 
only chaos and misery for the working class – an absurd paradox of the capitalist system.  
 
CC recommendation: Reject in favour of amendment 7 
 
7.​ Amend paragraph 26 (Durham) 
 
To the extent that it is adopted throughout the British economy, AI will render previously 
secure sectors redundant. Techno-optimists say AI investment will pay for itself by cutting 
labour costs, replacing up to 40 percent of tasks now done by humans in the not very distant 
future, and pushing jobless rates as high as 20 percent. The latest reports say that AI could 
destroy three million jobs in Britain, including many highly-skilled jobs, in the next decade.  
The absurd amount of overinvestment into AI has also raised alarm bells of a tech 
bubble 17 times larger than the dot-com bubble, which would have dire economic 
consequences should it burst. Without a planned economy, labour-saving technology 
creates only chaos and misery for the working class – an absurd paradox of the capitalist 
system. 
  
CC recommendation: Accept
